item.text: I’ve got enough material to synthesize. I’m not going to keep digging past the cap; this lens is heavily one-sided, with only weak counterevidence that the internet was restored after the protest wave ebbed.

**Bottom Line**
Mostly no. In 2024 Hasina’s government used internet shutdowns, information throttling, and arrest pressure to narrow political freedom. I found only one weak counterevidence item: connectivity was restored after the protest wave eased, but that looks reactive, not like a policy of protecting open political expression.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Freedom House: Bangladesh - Freedom on the Net 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024.  
  Claim: The Awami League manipulated the online information environment ahead of the January 2024 election, including blocking major news sites and throttling internet/communications around BNP rallies. This is direct evidence of digital control used to limit political freedom.  
  Question IDs: `4B.9`, also `4B.6`, `4B.5`, `4B.1`

- [Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) — Reuters, July 20, 2024.  
  Claim: Reuters reported soldiers in Dhaka, roadblocks, and a suspension of internet/text services as the government escalated against protesters. This is direct evidence of coercive administrative and digital control during political unrest.  
  Question IDs: `4B.9`, also `4B.6`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`

- [Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) — Reuters, July 22, 2024.  
  Claim: Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence, which points to coercive administrative control rather than open political space.  
  Question IDs: `4B.9`, also `4B.3`, `4B.5`, `4B.8`

- [Bangladesh's crackdown left more than 170 dead, U.N. says](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) — United Nations / OHCHR, July 26, 2024.  
  Claim: The UN said internet shutdowns reduce scrutiny and increase impunity. This is strong external confirmation that digital controls were being used to suppress oversight, not protect political freedom.  
  Question IDs: `4B.9`, also `4B.6`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`

- [Bangladesh repression, security force abuses discredit elections](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections) — Human Rights Watch, January 11, 2024.  
  Claim: HRW reported arrests for criticism, including social-media posts, plus repression and violence against opposition members before the January election. This is direct evidence of administrative harassment used to chill dissent.  
  Question IDs: `4B.9`, also `4B.6`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`, `4B.1`

- [Bangladesh restores internet as students call off jobquota protests](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-restores-internet-as-students-call-off-jobquota-protests-3540555) — Reuters, July 29, 2024.  
  Claim: Internet service was restored only after protesters called off the movement and conditions were said to be normalizing. This is the closest counterevidence, but it looks reactive and coercion-driven rather than proof that Hasina protected political freedom.  
  Question IDs: `4B.9`, also `4B.6`, `4B.3`

**Search Gap**
- I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Hasina used surveillance or digital policy to expand political freedom.
- The best positive material is only weak counterevidence after coercive disruption ended, not an affirmative pro-freedom pattern.
